question: Can a tuned LightGBM LambdaRank reranker on simple graph and dialogue-history features beat an embedding+MLP scorer at retrieving the answer entity per turn of a simulated conversation over a public KG?
method: Simulated 3000 four-turn conversations over FB15k-237 (follow-up vs topic-switch focus); candidates are 1-hop neighbours of all mentioned entities; conversation-level 75/25 split; hyper-parameters chosen by 3-fold grouped CV on train; both models evaluated once on test over all candidates, seeds 42-44.

dataset.name: FB15k-237 train triples, simulated conversational entity retrieval

baseline: Truncated-SVD entity/relation embeddings of the graph feeding an sklearn MLPClassifier that scores (history, relation, candidate) features.
improved: LightGBM LambdaRank reranker on graph/history features: relation match, recency of the matching source entity, ambiguity, degree, already-mentioned, relation-conditioned in-degree.
notes: n_rows/n_train/n_test count conversation turns (queries); graph has 272115 triples. Simulated stand-in, not the paper's CER-KG benchmark. Entities limited to degree <= 60; each asked (focus, relation) has a unique answer and the answer is never already mentioned, which makes 'already mentioned' an artefact-prone feature. Training/CV use the positive plus 20 sampled negatives per query (CV validation also on sampled candidates); test uses all candidates with pessimistic tie handling. The baseline is not given the focus entity and sees the graph only via embeddings; the tuning grids are small (2 configs each). Chosen params: {"baseline": "{'h': (64, 32), 'alpha': 0.001}", "improved": "{'n': 100, 'lr': 0.1, 'leaves': 15}"}. Data is simulated, so results do not transfer directly to real conversations.
